correctness.rationale: For a friendship graph with m triangles, every acyclic orientation is the independent choice of a total order within each triangle: 6^m choices. Condition on the common hub Gaussian rank U, uniform on [0,1]; the three triangle classes have individual ordered probabilities U²/2, (1-U)²/2 and U(1-U), each with two choices. Integrating their product gives the explicit integer-beta angle formula, and counting permutations of local types gives the multiplicities. For two directions, matching a triangle has kernel Q and all blocks match with conditional probability Q^m. The six-component probability vector has squared norm 1/2-2r+3r² with r=u(1-u), at most 1/2 and equal only at u=0,1. Hence Q has only two global maxima, both 1/2; its linear decrease Q=1/2-s-t+O((s+t)²) supplies exactly two 1/(4m²) local Laplace contributions. Exact independent all-permutation enumeration checked every cone frequency at m=1..4 and the collision values 1/6, 7/200, 167/19600, 23/9800. The analytic all-dimensional proof, not the finite tests, establishes the infinite claim.

value.rationale: This is a natural and completely specified infinite graph family with 6^m zonotope vertices. An exact per-vertex Euclidean normal-cone multiset is a complete geometrically meaningful invariant, and the two-sample collision moment predicts how often isotropic random objectives repeat vertices. The sharp asymptotic 2^{-m}/(2m²) is exponentially above the uniform benchmark 6^{-m}, with a rigorous two-corner rare-event explanation and a limiting distribution of the responsible hub ranks. The result is more than computing a few table entries or applying a generic theorem to a single object; it resolves a natural full-family metric distribution and its high-dimensional sampling behavior.
